thread.title: Dow Falls 1,000 Points In 2 Days | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Dow Falls 1,000 Points In 2 Days | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple, Microsoft, United Health and 3M led another pounding of blue chip issues as the Dow Jones industrial average, down 396 points on Monday, sank another 551 points (2.2%) on Tuesday to expand its two-day loss to as much as 1,055 points intraday, or 4.1%. The Nasdaq composite dropped 1.7%, the Nasdaq 100 slightly more than that.
X Some decent increases in earnings and sales for numerous big box retailers, including Best Buy ( BBY ) (fiscal Q3 earnings up 19% to 93 cents a share) and Ross Stores ( ROST ) (EPS up 26%), failed to cheer up Wall Street.
However, a handful of longtime market leaders, including HealthEquity ( HQY ), Square ( SQ ), Fortinet ( FTNT ), Atlassian ( TEAM ), Veeva Systems ( VEEV ), ServiceNow ( NOW ) and Palo Alto Networks ( PANW ), either gained ground or cut their losses sharply. Some of these names are also trying to stay near their long-term 200-day moving averages.
Before The Dow Jones Bottoms, Prepare For A New Uptrend This Way At this point, it's vital to wait and watch for evidence that these companies or others find a bottom and begin to form the right side of a new base . The minimum length of a cup with handle , for instance, is seven weeks. Yet a well-formed cup with handle , double bottom , flat base or base on base can take several months — or even up to a year — to finish.
When the market flashes a signal of a new confirmed uptrend , then breakouts from such chart patterns give individual investors a timely entry point to maximize reward and minimize risk.
Crude Oil Futures Burned Again Meanwhile, crude oil suffered more sharp losses. West Texas Intermediate crude prices at one point fell more than 7.7% to a session low of $52.77 a barrel amid growing concern that trade tariffs between the U.S. and China, plus uncertainty over the Brexit deal, may depress energy demand.
WTI crude futures have now fallen more than 30% beneath a year-to-date high of $76.90.
Watch for fresh weekly U.S. inventory data from the Energy Information Administration coming out on Wednesday, as noted in IBD's Econoday economic calendar .
Apple Drives The Dow Jones Industrials Lower Apple ( AAPL ), which had staged sterling gains ever since its Jan. 6, 2017 breakout from an early-stage base, a cup with handle, at 118.12, continues to make its biggest correction since its long decline in 2015 and 2016. The iPhone, iMac and digital services giant fell more than 5% and hit an intraday low of 175.51, extending its decline from a 233.47 all-time high to almost 25%. Investors are fretting a slowdown in growth of Apple's iPhone business.
Wall Street has shaved its long-term consensus profit estimates for the Cupertino, Calif., company. Analysts now see earnings rising just 13% to $13.48 a share in the current fiscal year that ends in September 2019 and up 10% in FY 2020 to $14.82.
On a quarterly basis, Apple's earnings have grown 2%, 11%, 18%, 24%, 16%, 30%, 40% and 41% vs. year-ago levels in the past eight quarters.
State Of The Nasdaq Composite At 6908, the tech-centered composite index has now dropped 15% from its all-time peak of 8133. That easily meets the definition of an intermediate-level correction.
During a true market correction, it's common to see top-performing stocks drop 1.5 to 2.5 times the decline in the major indexes. Apple reaffirms this tendency.
On Tuesday, losers smacked winners by more than a 3-1 margin on the Nasdaq, and nearly 6 to 1 on the NYSE.
This Dow Jones Component Continues To Fall Sharply Goldman Sachs ( GS ), a laggard for pretty much all year, slumped more than 6 points, or 3%, to around 191. The Wall Street bank and Dow Jones industrial average component is now 30% below its 52-week peak. The stock scores a mediocre 53 Composite Rating on a scale of 1 to 99 in IBD Stock Checkup .
Goldman and other money center banks have helped drag the S&P 500 down more than 1.8%. The 500, finishing the day at 2641, lies 10% beneath its 2940 peak.
The small-cap S&P 600 and the Russell 2000 fell 1.5% to 1.6%.
Money even came out of so-called defensive areas of Wall Street. The Dow utility average slipped nearly 0.5%. At 728, it holds a thin gain of less than 1% since Jan. 1. But investors are certainly loading up on long-dated U.S. Treasuries. The yield on the benchmark 10-year note is now currently at 3.05%, down sharply from a near-term high of 3.24%.
Meanwhile, Target ( TGT ) dropped more than 11% following a gap down at the open and staged an eighth straight loss. Shares traded as low as 66.12 and hit their lowest level since early January.
The major discount retail chain reported a 21% jump in third-quarter earnings to $1.09 a share, matching its biggest year-over-year increase in the past 20 quarters. After-tax margin improved by 30 basis points to 3.3%.
Revenue rose 6% to $17.59 billion.
